newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seen creating agriculture ambassador.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seen creating agriculture ambassador.

text.p: The Clinton administration is considering appointing an ambassador-level official at the U.S. Trade Representative's office to specialize in agricultural trade negotiations, a Congressional aide said Friday.
The aide to Iowa Democratic Sen Tom Harkin said he believed there was "a pretty good chance" that the post would be created.

Speaking to a joint convention of the American Soybean Association and the National Corn Growers Association the Senate aide said that Harkin talked with U.S. Trade Rep Charlene Barshefsky recently about an "agriculture ambassador" and that she seemed favorable.
"I think the odds are good... She (Barshevsky) seems quite committed to putting someone into a pretty prominent role," the aide said.
Such an appointment may require congressional approval.
Separately, a House Agriculture Committee staffer told the meeting that Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman was also looking at beefing up the staff at USDA working on international trade.
